profile.description: What this server registers and starts

models.description: What `--model` may be given, as the CLI offers it to the account in use

ServerProfile.description: What a server registers and starts, from `CLAUDIO_PROFILE`: `full` is the app; `headless` is an AI backend for one project, serving only the API routes such a client calls (docs/plans/headless-image.md, D1 and D2).

inUse.description: The account new work would start on, which is not always the CLI's own login: a signed-out default with a signed-in login account beside it still runs chats. Null when no account can take work

inUseReason.description: Why `inUse` is null: `signed-out` when no enabled account has a usable credential, `limit` when one has and every such account is at its limit. Null while `inUse` is set. Absent on an old server.

TokenSource.description: `wrapper-*`: configured through the API; `env-*`: passed through the container environment;

label.description: The alias, else the email, else the id

limit.description: The account's own reading: what the status bar draws for "Claude", never another account's

plan.description: Subscription type (`max`, `pro`, ...); null when none is known

AccountInUse.description: The account new work would start on, as Settings and the status bar name it

AccountKind.description: How an account signs in: `login` is `claude auth login` in the account's own config dir (it has an email, an organization and a plan); `token` is a `claude setup-token` and `api-key` an API key, which have no identity of their own, so they need an alias.

AccountSignInState.description: How far an account's sign-in can be trusted.

window.description: The window that binds (`five_hour`, `seven_day`), when it is known

utilization.description: Use of that window, 0..1; null when nothing was read

resetsAt.description: ISO time the binding window resets; null when unknown

observedAt.description: When the reading was taken: the cache can be days old, so the UI says how old

source.description: `stream`: a run reported it; `cli`: the CLI answered `get_usage`; `cache`: read from the account dir's `cachedUsageUtilization`; `failure`: a turn died on it

cli.description: The last `get_usage` answer, kept even when a newer stream reading supplied the windows: the per-model limits and the credits come from it only. Absent until the account was refreshed.

AccountLimit.description: One account's usage, folded from its stream events, the CLI's `get_usage` and, when idle, the CLI's cache.

ProviderLimitState.description: `unknown`: nothing was read, or the reset has passed since; never `ok` without a new reading.

observedAt.description: ISO time the CLI was asked

plan.description: Subscription type as the CLI states it (`max`, `pro`, `team`, `enterprise`); null for none

available.description: False for an API-key account: it has no subscription limits to read

AccountCliUsage.description: What only the CLI's `get_usage` control request states about an account; kept beside the folded windows.

model.description: The model's display name as the CLI states it (`Fable`)

window.description: The window it counts in; today always `seven_day`

ScopedRateLimit.description: A weekly limit that applies to one model only (`Fable`), beside the account-wide windows.

usedMinor.description: Spent this month, in minor units

limitMinor.description: The monthly cap in minor units; null when there is none

currency.description: ISO 4217 code; null when the CLI states none

exponent.description: Decimal places of the currency (2 for USD, EUR)

limitReached.description: The cap is reached: nothing more is spent until the month turns

disabledReason.description: Why the CLI says they are off, when it does

everEnabled.description: They were on once: tells "never set up" from "turned off"

AccountCredits.description: The usage credits of a subscription account: what it may spend beyond its plan limits. Amounts are in minor units (`1230` with `exponent: 2` is 12.30), as the CLI states them.

AccountInUseReason.description: Why no account can take new work now.

value.description: What the flag takes: an alias (`opus`) or a model's full name (`claude-fable-5-1[1m]`)

ids.description: The model ids an alias stands for, as chats that ran on it reported them (`claude-sonnet-5` for `sonnet`). Suggestions, moves and accepted mappings carry the id, the catalogue lists the alias: match a row on its `value` or on any of its `ids`. Absent where the value is already the id.

label.description: What the CLI calls it, where it says so; for an alias, the name of the model a chat started on it reported in its `system/init` event ("Sonnet 5" for `claude-sonnet-5`), once one has

description.description: The line the CLI shows under it

disabled.description: The CLI names it but cannot run it (it is too old for it, say); `description` says why

tier.description: How capable it is among its provider's models, where the provider says; a model with no rank has none

resolvedModel.description: The concrete model id behind `value` (`claude-opus-5-5` for `opus`), as the CLI's `initialize` reports it

supportsEffort.description: Whether the model takes an effort level at all

supportedEffortLevels.description: The effort levels it takes (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`); only these are offered for it

ModelTier.description: A provider's models by how fast or how strong they are; what model mapping across providers builds on.

ReadyStatus.description: `GET /api/ready`: 200 when ready, 503 with the reason otherwise. Says nothing more about the account

ReadyReason.description: Why a server is not ready to run a chat (`GET /api/ready`)

limits.description: The admission limits in force, so a screen can draw the point where no chat starts

SystemLoad.description: What the machine is doing now, read from `/proc`. A field the kernel does not expose here is null, never zero: a zero would read as an idle machine. `admitting` is false while a new chat would be refused for lack of memory, and `refusal` says why in words.

PressureReading.description: A kernel pressure reading (PSI): the share of the last 10 s in which some or every task waited, in percent.

cpuSome10.description: PSI `some10` of each resource, in percent

chats.description: Chats alive, and the resident memory of their process trees

admitting.description: Whether a new chat would have been admitted

SystemSample.description: One reading of the machine as the sampler stored it, once a minute (docs/resource-control.md). A figure the kernel did not give is null, never zero. In a bucketed answer the load, pressures, chats and resident memory are the largest of the bucket and `availableMb` the smallest: a chart of a quiet hour should still show the minute that was not.

processes.description: The processes of every chat, the CLIs included

ChatProcessUsage.description: What one chat's process tree uses: the CLI and every process it started. `rssMb` is resident memory summed over the tree and `cpuSeconds` the CPU time it has used so far; both are null where `/proc` cannot say. CPU use over a window is the difference between two readings, never one reading.

limits.description: One reading per provider that has one; Claude's is derived from the account in use (`accounts.inUse.limit`)

accounts.description: The account view every screen reads; absent until the server runs the accounts package

backgroundTasks.description: Commands and agents running in the background, whichever chat sent them

workflows.description: Claude Code workflows running right now

window.description: The window that binds (`5h`, `7d`, `primary`), when the provider names windows

utilization.description: Use of that window, 0..1; null when the provider reports none

resetsAt.description: ISO time the binding window resets; null when unknown

overage.description: Extra usage past the plan's window, when the reading says anything about it

observedAt.description: When the reading was taken: the UI says how old it is

source.description: `stream`: a live run reported it; `probe`: a read that spends nothing; `failure`: a turn died on it

ProviderLimit.description: One provider's usage limit, folded from what its driver reports.

ProviderId.description: An agent provider, by the id its manifest declares (`claude-code`). A string and not a closed union, so adding a provider is adding a folder in core and never a change here.

using.description: The run is being served from overage now

resetsAt.description: ISO time the overage resets; null when unknown

disabledReason.description: Why overage is not available, as the provider words it

ProviderLimitOverage.description: The overage side of a limit reading: whether the account is spending past its window, and until when.

inUse.description: The account new work would start on: the pin-less choice, which honours `settings.preferred`; null when none can take work

inUseReason.description: Why `inUse` is null; null while it is set

accounts.description: Every account, the CLI's own login left out while it has no credential

atLimit.description: Every enabled, signed-in account is out (exhausted, with its reset ahead or unknown)

nextReset.description: ISO time of the earliest reset among the accounts that are out; null when none is or none gave one

AccountView.description: The accounts as every screen reads them, computed once (`Core.accountView()`): the account new work starts on, the list, and whether every account that could take work is out. `GET /auth.inUse` and `overview.accounts` are this view, so the status bar, the chip and the cards cannot disagree.

alias.description: Shown instead of the email; required for `token` and `api-key`, which have no identity

email.description: From `claude auth status`; null for `token` and `api-key`

plan.description: Subscription type (`max`, `pro`, ...); null when the CLI reports none

enabled.description: A disabled account is never chosen for new work

signedIn.description: `claude auth status` says it is logged in

signInState.description: Whether the sign-in can be relied on: `expired` after a run on it failed to authenticate, `incomplete` when its credentials file has no refresh token (a broken copy), `ok` when neither is so and the account is signed in, `unknown` when nothing says either way. Anything but `ok` or `unknown` makes `signedIn` false.

authFailedAt.description: ISO time a run on it failed because the CLI could not authenticate; cleared when the account signs in again. Absent while it can authenticate

checkedAt.description: When the credential was last checked with `get_usage` (no turn) or a test message; null when never

Account.description: One Claude account: a config directory of its own, chosen per process.

rotateOnLimit.description: Switch account at a limit; off waits for the reset instead

threshold.description: Utilization (0-100) of an account's binding window from which it counts as at its limit

hysteresis.description: Points (0-100) below the threshold an account must fall before it is chosen again

cooldownSeconds.description: Seconds an account is left alone after a rejection that gave no reset (or one of extra usage): recorded on that account's reading, which reads exhausted until then

preferred.description: The account new work starts on while it has room and the chat's policy allows it; null leaves the choice to the strategy. A pin wins over it, and a project policy that does not list it too. `PUT /accounts/settings` accepts an enabled account's id.

order.description: The global order of the accounts, which the `order` strategy follows; empty means the order they are listed in. `PUT /accounts/settings` accepts every enabled account's id once (disabled ones may be listed too); an account added later goes after the ones named.

AccountsSettings.description: `accounts.json`: when and how work moves to another account.

AccountStrategy.description: Which account new work takes among the eligible ones.

id.description: The session id

provider.description: The provider that runs the chat; a chat read from Claude's transcripts is `claude-code`

providerSessionId.description: The id the provider chose for its own session; null on Claude, where the chat id is the session id

project.description: Null for a loose chat: its directory is under no imported project

orchestration.description: The orchestration it works for, when its origin is `orchestration`

derivedFrom.description: Set on a fork: where it started from

atLimit.description: The chat's last turn died on its provider's usage limit. Kept in the server's memory only: after a restart it is absent, and the page falls back on the provider's reading.

account.description: Id of the  {@link  Account }  the chat's last process ran on, or the one it was switched to; absent without accounts

pendingAccount.description: The account a person chose while a turn was running: it takes over when the turn ends; null when none waits

alive.description: Whether a process still holds the chat: an execution of Claudio's, or a terminal's or another program's. Nothing delegated from a chat that is not alive can be running, so every screen that would show a spinner for a branch asks this first.

execution.description: The live execution, when Claudio has a process on the chat; also the last of `executions`

activity.description: What that execution is doing right now; `null` whenever none is live

context.description: Null until the chat has had a response

tools.description: What it was started with, when Claudio started it: absent for a chat born in a terminal

pending.description: Messages sent to it that the agent has not taken yet, oldest first, and those lost on the way since; only while Claudio has a record of the chat (docs/chat-delivery.md)

claudioAssistant.description: Set on a chat of the Claudio assistant: it keeps its confinement whenever it is continued, resumed or forked

guards.description: The guards on its live process; absent when none runs or the chat is not guarded (docs/plans/guards.md)

policy.description: The policy of a confined API chat, fixed at its creation; null for any other chat (docs/plans/headless-image.md, D14)

teammateReads.description: Which teammates' shared copies its agent may read now (docs/plans/collaborators-agent-access.md); null when it may read none. Only on a chat read alone, decided on its live process

ChatSummary.description: A chat as the list shows it: everything but what only its own page needs, which costs a read of its transcript and its sidecar files per chat.

ChatProject.description: The project a chat belongs to.

exists.description: False once the worktree is removed: history, never a place to start a chat

ChatWorktree.description: The git worktree a chat works in, when it is not the project's own checkout.

ChatOrigin.description: Where a chat was born. Never changes, even when resuming adopts the chat. `api`: a request to the OpenAI-compatible surface (`POST /v1/chat/completions`) started it; like `internal` and the workers, it is left out of the chat lists unless asked for, and it expires with its conversation.

role.description: What the chat does for the graph; `task` is the only role with a taskId

ChatOrchestration.description: The orchestration a chat works for.

OrchestrationChatRole.description: What a chat does for the orchestration it works for.

ChatState.description: What is happening in a chat right now, whoever is driving it.

ChatControl.description:
What a person can do with a chat right now, and why not when they cannot. Where the chat was born says nothing about this: an `external` chat nobody holds is `resumable`.

`readOnly` always says why in words a person reads, and names the one way forward: `fork` continues in a copy, `hint` (a task that is still running) sends the worker a nudge from the orchestration board without typing into its conversation.

error.description: Why it failed, when it did

cause.description: `rate-limit` when the turn died on its account's limit, as the CLI reported it in data (a rejected `rate_limit_event`, or a result with a 429); absent otherwise and on an execution recorded before it was kept. The error's wording is never read for it. `auth` when it died on its account's sign-in (a result with a 401): the account is marked signed out, which is what the rotation passes over, so it does not count among the accounts a limit passed over.

account.description: Id of the  {@link  Account }  its process ran on; null or absent for one recorded before accounts, or run on the CLI's own default login

effort.description: The effort its process was started with; absent when none was passed (the CLI's default, or a provider without effort) and on an execution recorded before it was kept

maxBudgetUsd.description: Ceiling on what it could spend

costUsd.description: Null when the CLI reported none: cost is only known for what Claudio launched

modelCosts.description: What the CLI reported per model (`modelUsage[model].costUSD`), the only honest split of `costUsd`: absent on an execution recorded before Claudio kept it or one the CLI reported none for.

Execution.description: One stretch of a chat during which Claudio had a process working on it; a chat has several and at most one is live.

ExecutionOutcome.description: How an execution ended. `interrupted`: its process was lost (the wrapper restarted or crashed) rather than stopped or finished.

TokenUsage.description: Tokens counted in the four ways the API bills them.

kind.description: `tool`: a tool call without its result yet; `writing`/`thinking`: a text or thinking block is streaming; `waiting`: blocked on a permission prompt

tool.description: The CLI's tool name (`Edit`, `Bash`, `Grep`, `Task`…) when `kind` is `tool`

target.description: A short human label for the tool's input: a path relative to the chat's cwd, a command's description or its first 80 characters, a pattern, a subagent's description, a URL's host

ChatActivity.description: What a live execution is doing right now, from its latest stream-json events.

used.description: Tokens the last response read: `input + cache`. A snapshot, so compaction shows as a drop.

window.description: The model's context window; null when the model is not known, so no percentage is invented

compactedSince.description: Set only while the newest compaction boundary is later than the last main response: the meter shows `postTokens` at once instead of waiting for the next response

ChatContext.description: How full the conversation is, as of its last response.

usd.description: Null when there is no figure to give (a chat started from a terminal): read as "not available"

tokens.description: Everything the chat spent, subagents included, split by model

ChatCost.description: What a chat has cost. Only real data: nothing is estimated from a price table.

model.description: Model id, variant suffix included; null for messages that did not say

ChatModelTokens.description: Tokens counted the four ways the API bills them, for one model.

preset.description: The preset in force, when one was chosen; editing a preset later does not change a live chat

mcp.description: Null when the chat takes whatever the CLI loads on its own

policy.description: The policy the chat was started with, so a resume enforces the same one

claudioMcp.description: Claudio's own MCP server (all its tools, under the chat's permission mode), switched on from the chat's "+" or its start options: every process of the chat starts with it, a resume, a fork and Claudio's own respawns included. Absent reads off.

ChatToolConfig.description: What a chat is running with, shown on its detail because it is what explains a refusal.

description.description: One line saying what it is for, shown next to the name when picking

policy.description: What a shipped preset states in Claudio's words; each provider translates it into its own rules

builtIn.description: Shipped with Claudio. Editable like any other, but a fresh install has it again.

ToolPreset.description: A named set of `--allowedTools` / `--disallowedTools`, picked when a chat starts or resumes.

edit.description: Paths are relative to the project; `deny` is denial outright, for a mode that would otherwise ask

exclusive.description: Nothing outside the policy exists for the session: no person's settings, hooks or servers

ToolPolicy.description: What a session may do, in Claudio's words. Each provider's driver translates it into its own rules and lists the parts it cannot enforce.

CommandRule.description: A shell command a policy allows or denies, in Claudio's words.

servers.description: Names of configured servers, as `GET /config/mcp` lists them; empty starts the chat with none

config.description: Path of the config file Claudio wrote for the CLI, reported back so a chat can be explained

McpSelection.description: Which of the configured MCP servers a chat starts with. Claudio writes the file the CLI reads and passes it as `--mcp-config` / `--strict-mcp-config`; there is no other way in.

text.description: The words, without the framing Claudio wraps around a hint or a notice for the agent

source.description: Who it comes from; `person` for a message stored before it was recorded

blockedBy.description: On a `written` message, while the turn waits on a foreground call the agent will not read it before

ChatPendingMessage.description: A message the agent has not taken yet, or one it never will. `written`: in the agent's own queue, read at its next tool boundary or as its next turn. `held`: waiting for the process that replaces one on its way out. `undelivered`: lost on the way, with `reason`.

ChatPendingAttachment.description: A file sent with a message, as the page shows it: no path on the server's disk.

ChatMessageSource.description: Who a message written into a chat comes from. `person`: someone typed it (a message, a hint from the page). `supervisor`: the Supervisor sent it on its own, as a hint. `claudio`: Claudio wrote it for its own reasons, such as telling the agent a command was cancelled. Only a person's message is the person's to hurry ("Send now"); the others are notices.

name.description: The tool, as the agent names it: `Agent`, `Task`, `Bash`

description.description: What it does, in the agent's words: the agent's description, or the command

ChatPendingBlocker.description: The call the agent's turn is inside of, which it reads no message before it returns: a foreground agent (`Agent`, `Task`) or a command. It can be sent to the background (`POST /chats/:id/commands/:toolUseId/background`), which returns it at once and lets the message in.

projectId.description: The project in scope when the chat started: context, not a requirement

language.description: The language the assistant answers in, read from `Accept-Language` when the chat started

ClaudioAssistantMarker.description: What a Claudio assistant chat remembers about what it is, so the core re-applies its confinement and its guide on every process, whatever a request asks.

ClaudioLanguage.description: The languages Claudio speaks. A chat Claudio starts on its own is listed by the first line of its prompt, so that line is written in the person's language, read from the request's `Accept-Language` (`claudioLanguage`) and kept on what runs later or again (an assistant run, a flow run); the instructions for Claude after it may stay in English.

rules.description: The effective rules, in the order they run

ChatGuards.description: The guards on a chat's live process (`Chat.guards`). `arming`: waiting for the guard's session marker before the first prompt; `armed`: live; `missing`: a tool call went by unguarded and the run was interrupted; `off`: the chat is not guarded.

GuardRuleId.description: A rule of the guard program. `integrity` protects the guard itself; it is a rule like the others (D6 of docs/plans/regression-fixes-2026-10-29.md), on by default, and a guard with no rule on is no guard at all. `declared-tools` confines a confined API chat to the tools and paths it declared (docs/plans/headless-image.md, D14.5); it is armed by the chat's launch from its stored policy, never by a setting.

GuardMode.description: `enforce` blocks; `observe` records "would block" and passes, for rollback after a false positive.

workspaceId.description: The workspace it runs in, null for one in a working directory

allowedTools.description: The declared Claude Code permission rules; the only tools it has (`--tools`)

maxBudgetUsd.description: What it may spend; `CLAUDIO_CHAT_BUDGET_USD` when the request named none

ApiChatPolicy.description: What a confined API chat runs under, fixed when it is created and stored with it (docs/plans/headless-image.md, D14): every chat of a headless Claudio, and every chat in a workspace in any profile. Resume, fork and settings changes are not served for such a chat.

AgentReadScope.description: Why a chat may read teammates' copies through its token (docs/plans/collaborators-agent-access.md): `assistant` reads every copy whose sharer allows it, `project` only those of its own project.

detail.description: Model reply, or the CLI error

gitUrl.description: Clone this repository instead of creating an empty directory

template.description: Configures the project from a template; without one, and without `modules`, every module is off

modules.description: The modules to switch on; when given, it replaces the template's choice instead of adding to it

ProjectTemplateId.description: The built-in templates. `simple` switches nothing on and `custom` starts from everything off for the person to choose; the other three are presets. There are no user-saved templates.

hits.description: Hits in transcript order, oldest first: one per entry, however many times it matches

total.description: Entries searched, the same `total` a page of the transcript reports

truncated.description: More entries matched than `hits` carries; the oldest ones were left out

index.description: Index of the entry or event, in the same index space as `from` and `total` of a page

snippet.description: The text around the first match, whitespace collapsed

TranscriptSearchHit.description: One entry whose text contains the query.

text.description: For `partial`, `result`, `stderr`, `notice` and `other` events; for `other`, a stdout line the driver could not read

block.description: For `partial` events: which kind of block is streaming

append.description: For `partial` events after the first of a block: text to append at `at` (the length the client must hold)

init.description: For `init` events, in the provider's neutral words

data.description: For `notice` events only: Claudio's own words, never a provider's

delivery.description: For `delivery` events: what became of one message the person sent

guard.description: For `guard` events: what the guard said about one tool call, so a live viewer can show a block without polling

RunEventKind.description: `partial` events are ephemeral: they carry the block being streamed (the first one of a block, and the first a subscriber receives, all the text so far in `text`; the rest only what is new, in `append`, with where it starts in `at`), reuse the seq of the last stored event, are never buffered or replayed, and are superseded by the next `message` event.

compaction.description: Set on the CLI's compaction marker (`blocks` is empty) and on the summary it continued from; both have `role: 'user'` and are not the person's words

ToolResultDetail.description: What the CLI recorded beside a tool result (`tool_use_result` on its stream, `toolUseResult` in its transcript), kept only where it says something the result's text does not: the text stays the record, this tells the page how to read it.

TranscriptCompaction.description: A compaction as the transcript records it: the CLI's marker, or the summary it continued from

tools.description: The names of the tools the session has, as the provider calls them

RunInit.description: What a session reports about itself when it starts.

cause.description: Why a failed result is not one to try again blindly: the budget ran out, the account hit its limit or someone stopped it.

subtype.description: The provider's own word for how the turn ended, when it gave one (Claude Code's result `subtype`: `success`, `error_max_turns`, `error_max_budget_usd`…). `/v1` names a turn that ended without its answer from it (D16 of docs/plans/headless-image.md).

stopReason.description: The main agent's last stop reason in the turn (`end_turn`, `tool_use`, `max_tokens`…), when the provider said

taskId.description: Absent for a change of the whole list

RunTaskChange.description: A background task starting, moving or ending, or the whole list being replaced.

source.description: Who the message comes from; absent on events streamed before it was recorded, which were a person's

reason.description: For `undelivered`, when the page has something to do about it besides showing the sentence of `message.reason`

at.description: For `delivered`: when the agent took it, which for a message read mid-turn is later than when it was sent

MessageDelivery.description: What became of one message sent to a chat, by its id (docs/chat-delivery.md). `delivered`: the agent took it, into the running turn or as a turn of its own, at `at`. `undelivered`: its process went away first, the one that should have read it could not start, the agent went on without it (`reason: 'not-read'`) or it was withdrawn (`reason: 'cancelled'`); `message` carries it, so the page can hand it back. `carried`: a move or a limit replay sent it on, to `chatId` (this chat on a replay), under the same id.

MessageUndeliveredReason.description: Why a message ended `undelivered`, for the page to act on. `cancelled`: withdrawn from the agent's queue before it read it (`DELETE /chats/:id/messages/:messageId`). `not-read`: the agent went on without it: its queue no longer held it after an interrupt or a result, and it never read it back.

excerpt.description: The command or path, masked, at most 240 characters

GuardOutcome.description: What became of one guarded tool call. `blocked` and `observed` are the guard's verdicts; `missing` is a tool call with no guard marker, `unarmed` a run that started without the guard being live, `error` a guard that failed and so blocked, `allowed-once` a block a person let through once in an interactive chat.

chatId.description: The chat whose start reported it

EffectiveEnvironment.description: What Claude Code actually loaded for a directory, taken from the `init` event of the most recent chat Claudio started there (the CLI only reports it when a session starts).

output.description: Without `offset`, the tail of the file (at most 64 KiB); with it, up to 64 KiB of what follows that byte, so a longer gap takes several reads (`offset` < `bytes` means more is waiting)

truncated.description: `output` is the tail of a longer file, not its start. Never set on a read that resumed from `offset`.

bytes.description: Size of the output file in bytes

offset.description: Byte position just after `output`: pass it back as `?offset=` to read only what came since

reset.description: The requested `offset` was past the end of the file (it was replaced), so `output` restarts from the tail

BackgroundTaskOutput.description: Captured output of a background task, as the CLI wrote it.

workflowRunId.description: The workflow run (`wf_…`) a workflow agent belongs to

description.description: The description given at launch; a workflow agent's is its label

prompt.description: Its first message: the prompt it was given

status.description: `stopped` when its session ended before the agent reported back; `waiting` when it ended its turn with background work of its own running

durationMs.description: Time it was active, over all its runs; the current run's elapsed time is `runs` against the clock

runs.description: Every stretch it worked, oldest first; empty for a workflow agent

result.description: Text of the agent's last assistant message: what it reported back

entries.description: Entries of the transcript, from index `from` on (all of it unless `?after=` asked for a tail)

from.description: Index of the first entry returned

total.description: Entries in the whole transcript: pass it back as `?after=` to read only what was appended

tasks.description: Background tasks this agent launched, where the transcripts say so (subagents only)

HealthSignalKind.description:
What a signal noticed. FlowRunOutcome.description: How a run ended: `passed`, it finished well (and for QA, the item held); `rejected`, QA's verdict failed the item; `failed`, the chat failed or its result was unreadable; `cancelled`, a person's move or the flow being switched off made it moot before it started.

FlowRunQueuedBy.description: Who queued a flow run by hand, when a card entering its column did not.

chatId.description: Set once its chat started; null for a run with nothing to read

supersedes.description: The run whose pending proposals this one superseded when it started, which reads again

AssistantRunEvent.description: An assistant run started, read something, ended or failed.

AssistantRunKind.description: `project`: team, resources and first work items, after creating a project or on demand from its page. `work-items`: "Suggest tasks" on the board. `resources`: "Suggest" on the Resources tab, or "Create with AI" for one resource from a description. `evals`: "Draft cases" in an eval's editor (Phase 2).

AssistantRunAction.description: `started` and `failed` as they say; `ended` a run that completed or was stopped (its `status` says which); `read` a running one's  {@link  AssistantRun.sources } , cost or  {@link  AssistantRunDetail.draft }  changed, at most every few seconds, so "what it has read" and the file "Create with AI" writes fill in without polling.

AssistantRunStatus.description: `running` has its chat, or is about to; `completed` answered and its proposals are served; `failed` ended without a readable answer (the chat failed, the result did not match the schema, or a restart cut it and it could not be started again); `stopped` a person stopped it. A finished run never runs again: "Suggest again" is a new run.

AssistantProposalEvent.description: A proposal was accepted, discarded or restored. What an accept wrote announces itself too where it has an event (`workitem.created`, `team.changed`); a saved resource has none, so this names it.

AssistantResourceKind.description: The resources an assistant proposes or creates: the ones a project's `.claude/` holds as Markdown.

ConfigScopeKind.description: Every /config route takes an optional `?project=<projectId>`: absent means the user scope (the Claude config dir), present means that project's own files.

SettingsChangedEvent.description: A layered setting changed, from the UI or the file: the whole document as it now stands.

allowedHosts.description: Host names this wrapper answers to besides loopback, each a name or a `*.domain` pattern with at least two labels below the wildcard. Read, it is the configured allowlist: the environment's hosts followed by the ones added in the UI. Written (`PUT`), it is the UI's part only, which adds to the environment's: a host the environment already names is not stored again. The exact names a running tunnel adds for itself are in neither, because nobody may edit them.

maxConcurrentRuns.description: How many runs may work at once; a change applies to the next run, without a restart

defaultPermissionMode.description: The `--permission-mode` of a run that does not ask for one; applies to the next run

setupSeen.description: The setup assistant was finished or skipped. Kept here rather than in the browser so a second browser, a phone or the desktop app does not ask again. It replaces `providersStepSeen`: that stored value and its variable, `CLAUDIO_PROVIDERS_STEP_SEEN`, still count.

dailySpendCapUsd.description: What all of Claudio's automation may spend in a local day, in USD, summing the cost the CLI reports for each result. A start gate, not a kill switch: over it new automated work waits and nothing running is stopped. Null (the default) is no cap; otherwise above 0 and at most 100,000, in cents.

evalsPhase2.description: Instruction evals, Phase 2: pressure levels, judged expectations, the promotion gate and case drafting. Off by default; while off, those routes answer 409 `evals-phase2-off`. Phase 1 evals are not affected.

openaiToolCallTimeoutMinutes.description: How long the OpenAI-compatible surface holds a client's tool call, in minutes, from the end of the turn that handed it over until the client's next request brings the result. A call still owed then is answered to the CLI with an error result, and the chat is stopped. A whole number from 1 to 1440, 10 by default; a `PUT` with `null` resets it to the default.

sources.description: For `allowedHosts`, the highest layer that names any host (`env`, then `file`, then `default`); it does not make the list read-only, `allowedHostLayers` does that per host.

AppSettings.description: `GET /settings/app`: every layered setting, and where each one's value comes from.

AppSettingSource.description: Where a layered setting's current value comes from. `env` means the UI may show it but not change it, except for `allowedHosts`, whose layers add up instead of replacing one another: there `env` only says the environment names some of the hosts, and `allowedHostLayers` tells which.

env.description: From `CLAUDIO_ALLOWED_HOSTS`: fixed by whoever deployed the install, read-only in the UI

file.description: From `app-settings.json`: added in the UI, and what a `PUT` of `allowedHosts` replaces

runtime.description: Exact names lent while their owner runs (a running tunnel's host): memory only, never editable

AllowedHostLayers.description: The hosts the guard answers to besides loopback, by who put each one there. Unlike the other settings, the layers add up: what the guard answers is all three together.

widgets.description: In the order they are drawn within their area

config.description: What this instance was set up with; each widget type reads only the keys it knows

title.description: One line a notification can show as it is

TunnelChangedEvent.description: The tunnel moved to another state, got a new address, or had its settings changed. Carries the whole status, so a client that follows the feed never has to refetch it.

url.description: The tailnet HTTPS address (`https://<node>.<tailnet>.ts.net:<port>`), reachable only from the person's own tailnet; null unless `state` is `active`, so nobody is sent to one that does not answer yet

since.description: When the tunnel last became active; null unless `state` is `active`

reason.description: Why the tunnel failed, with a code a client translates; null unless `state` is `failed`, or `active` after ten minutes of readings that Tailscale did not answer (`tunnel.tailscaleNotAnswering`)

checking.description: The last readings of Tailscale got no answer (a timeout or a spawn failure on a busy machine): the tunnel stays `active` with its rule and host, and the UI says "Checking…"

enabled.description: Whether this deploy offers the tunnel at all (`CLAUDIO_TUNNEL`, on by default). While false, `start` is refused and the UI says who can turn it on instead of offering a button

managed.description: Whether the `tailscaled` behind the CLI is Claudio's own: the one the Docker image starts in userspace networking, with its state on the data volume (`CLAUDIO_TAILSCALE_MANAGED`). Only then does the app sign it in and out (`POST /setup/logins` with `tool: 'tailscale'`); a machine's own Tailscale is the person's, and the UI says what to run instead

tailscale.description: Whether Tailscale can carry the tunnel, and if not, why; the UI shows nothing else until it is `ready`

port.description: The HTTPS port on the tailnet name that Claudio's Serve rule uses: the rule's own while one stands, else the one the next start takes (`settings.port`, or `CLAUDIO_TUNNEL_PORT`; 8444 by default)

portSource.description: Where `port` comes from: `env` (`CLAUDIO_TUNNEL_PORT`, read-only here), `file` or `default`

portTaken.description: While `failed` with `tunnel.portTaken`: what holds the port, and the next free one

TunnelState.description: `starting`: Claudio is adding its Serve rule. `verifying`: the rule was sent, and Claudio reads the node's Serve config back to make sure it holds and points at this server before showing the address.

code.description: Stable across releases: a translation is keyed by it

Localized.description: A sentence the server writes, with a stable key beside it. The API answers in English and reads as it is; a client that knows the code says the same thing in its own language, and one that does not shows `text`.

version.description: The CLI's version (`tailscale version`, first line); null when there is no CLI to ask

host.description: This node's MagicDNS name, without the trailing dot; null until the daemon reports one

reason.description: What is missing, with a code a client translates; null while `ready`

holder.description: What holds it, from `tailscale serve status --json`, in a few words: the address and where it forwards to (another Claudio shows as its own `127.0.0.1:<port>`), a TCP forwarder, or a `tailscale serve` running in a terminal

nextFree.description: The first port above it that the node's Serve config leaves free; null when there is none

TunnelPortTaken.description: The port a start found serving something else (`tunnel.portTaken`).

startWithClaudio.description: Open the tunnel whenever Claudio starts; off unless the person turns it on

port.description: The HTTPS port of Claudio's Serve rule on the tailnet name, 1024–65535, 8444 by default. Changed only while the tunnel is stopped or failed, and read-only where `CLAUDIO_TUNNEL_PORT` sets it

TunnelSettings.description: What the tunnel may be told to do beside starting and stopping it (`tunnel-settings.json`).

title.description: One line a notification can show as it is

LanChangedEvent.description: The listener on the local network opened, closed, was refused, failed, changed its addresses or had its settings changed. Carries the whole status; never a notification.

reason.description: Why it is `refused`, `port-in-use` or `failed`, with a code a client translates; null otherwise

port.description: The port it listens on, or would

addresses.description: Where devices open it; empty unless `listening`

interfaces.description: The machine's IPv4 interfaces, loopback left out, to choose `bind` from

available.description: Whether it may listen here at all: false where `CLAUDIO_LAN=off`

portTaken.description: While `port-in-use`: what holds the port (the address it was taken on) and the next free one

LanState.description: `off`: not listening. `refused`: it should listen, but the guard asks for no credential (`mode: none`). `port-in-use`: something else on the machine holds the port. `failed`: the listener could not open for another reason (an address the machine no longer has, say).

ip.description: The IPv4 address the listener answers on; for a `.local` name, the one it resolved to

host.description: `<hostname>.local` when it resolves to one of the listening addresses; null for the bare address

LanAddress.description: An address a device on the network opens Claudio at.

name.description: The operating system's name for it (`wlp2s0`, `eth0`)

LanInterface.description: A network interface of the machine with an IPv4 address the listener could bind to.

enabled.description: Whether it listens whenever Claudio starts. `null` is the launcher's default (`CLAUDIO_LAN`): on for the desktop app (`auto`) and with `on`, off where nothing set it. A status always says what applies (a boolean); a `PUT` with `null` goes back to the default.

port.description: 1024–65535, 8791 by default; read-only where `CLAUDIO_LAN_PORT` sets it

bind.description: Every IPv4 address of the machine, or the ones listed; read-only where `CLAUDIO_LAN_BIND` sets it

LanSettings.description: `lan-settings.json`: whether, where and on which port the listener opens.

TerminalChangedEvent.description: A terminal opened, ended or changed, or the settings changed. Carries the summary, never output.

TerminalScope.description: What a terminal is opened in: a project's directory or worktree, a chat's working directory, or the workspace where chats outside any project run.

peerCheck.description: `unknown` when the peer process could not be found, which is not the same as "not a chat"

TerminalUnavailableReason.description: Why the terminal cannot be opened from here and now; `null` in the status when it can.

shell.description: The shell's path; `null` is the person's login shell

TerminalRemote.description: Which devices may open a terminal beyond this machine: none, the tunnel with a token, or any.

WebhookChangedEvent.description: A registration was created, adopted, tested, re-pointed, changed state or was removed. Carries the whole registration.

id.description: Claudio's id for it; the receiver's address ends with it

remoteHookId.description: The host's id for the hook, as text so a 64-bit id never loses precision

url.description: Where the host delivers: the public address plus the receiver's path

events.description: The event names the hook subscribes to, in the host's words

lastResponse.description: The host's own report of the last delivery; null until it said

notice.description: Only in the answer that registered it, in words for the person: another Claudio install's hook is on the repository and was left alone. Never stored.

WebhookRegistration.description: A hook Claudio registered on a project's repository. The secret that signs its deliveries is kept on the server and is never part of this document.

WebhookState.description: Where a registered hook stands. `active`: it delivers, or has not failed yet. `failing`: the host reports its last delivery as refused or unanswered. `stale`: its URL is no longer Claudio's public address and Claudio could not re-point it. `removed`: the person removed it.

WebhookLastResponse.description: What the host last answered when it delivered to the hook, as it reports it.

LoginUpdatedEvent.description: A sign-in moved: it started, showed its code, or ended. Carries the URL and the code and never anything else the CLI printed.

host.description: The host or address it signs in to; null for an agent

url.description: The page the person opens, for a device sign-in once the CLI printed it

code.description: The code the person types there. Null for Tailscale, whose login URL is the whole sign-in: the person opens it and approves, with nothing to type

expiresAt.description: When a live sign-in stops waiting: 15 minutes after it started

ready.description: What the tool's readiness said once the sign-in ended: true signed in, false not, null when the vendor offers no probe or it was not read

LoginSession.description: One sign-in, as `POST /setup/logins` started it. Never carries the key or anything else the CLI printed.

LoginMethod.description: `key`: a key or token the person pastes. `device`: the vendor's device-code sign-in, where the person opens a URL on their own device and types the code Claudio shows.

LoginErrorCode.description: Why a sign-in failed, as a code and never as what the CLI printed. `cli-missing`: the tool's binary was not found. `spawn-failed`: it could not be started. `cli-refused`: the CLI exited with an error. `no-code`: a device sign-in ended before it showed a URL and a code. `not-signed-in`: the command finished but the tool's readiness still says signed out. `timeout`: a key login did not finish in time and was stopped.

resetsAt.description: The next local midnight (ISO 8601), when the day's spend starts again from zero

unreported.description: Results today that carried no cost, which the sum cannot include

byAccountKind.description: For subscription accounts (`login`, `token`) the figure is the API price of the use, not a bill

SpendState.description: Today's spend against the cap (`GET /spend`), in the server's local day.

SpendLevel.description: Follows the usage bars: neutral below 60 %, warn from 60 %, bad from 75 %, exhausted at 100 %; off with no cap.

EvalSampleOutcome.description: Only `passed` and `failed` are scored; the rest say why a sample says nothing about the target. `unjudged` (Phase 2): a judge failed, so the judged expectation has no verdict; it fails closed for the gate.

path.description: How the connection to the owner travels while connected

error.description: The last pull failed, with a code a client translates; null when it did not

CollaboratorsJoinRequestEvent.description: A join reached the owner's install and waits for an answer; only the owner's install emits it.

from.description: The joiner's endpoint id, the `:from` of the accept and deny routes

relayedBy.description: The member that relayed it while the owner was offline; null when it came straight to the owner

JoinRequest.description: A join waiting for the owner's answer, on the owner's install (`GET /collaborators/groups/:id/join-requests`).

JoinAnswer.description: How a join request on the owner's install was settled.

CollaboratorsJoinEndedEvent.description: A join this install sent ended without joining: the owner denied it, or its invite expired before the owner answered. Only the joiner's install emits it; the page shows the ended join until dismissed.

groupName.description: The group's name, as the invite carried it

relayedBy.description: The member holding the request until the owner is back; null while it is still being delivered

expiresAt.description: The invite's expiry: past it the owner refuses the request

endedAt.description: When this install learnt it was denied or saw the invite expire; null while it waits

PendingJoin.description: A `join` this install sent: waiting for the owner, or ended without joining until it is dismissed.

PendingJoinState.description: Where a join this install sent stands: `waiting` for the owner, `denied` by the owner, or `expired` because the invite ran out before the owner answered. A join the owner accepted is no longer pending: the group is listed instead.

lastEventId.description: Id of the newest event the server has emitted

bootId.description: Changes on every server start; ids restart from 1 with it, so a new one means a full resync

version.description: The Claudio version the server runs; a page built for another one is out of date

StreamHelloEvent.description: Sent first on every connection, without an SSE id: it is not part of the replay buffer.

StreamResyncEvent.description: Sent instead of a replay when the client's `Last-Event-ID` is not one this server can continue from (it fell out of the buffer, or is newer than anything emitted, as after a restart): whatever the client cached may be stale, so it must refetch everything live.

id.description: The session id

provider.description: The provider that runs the chat; a chat read from Claude's transcripts is `claude-code`

providerSessionId.description: The id the provider chose for its own session; null on Claude, where the chat id is the session id

project.description: Null for a loose chat: its directory is under no imported project

orchestration.description: The orchestration it works for, when its origin is `orchestration`

derivedFrom.description: Set on a fork: where it started from

atLimit.description: The chat's last turn died on its provider's usage limit. Kept in the server's memory only: after a restart it is absent, and the page falls back on the provider's reading.

account.description: Id of the  {@link  Account }  the chat's last process ran on, or the one it was switched to; absent without accounts

pendingAccount.description: The account a person chose while a turn was running: it takes over when the turn ends; null when none waits

alive.description: Whether a process still holds the chat: an execution of Claudio's, or a terminal's or another program's. Nothing delegated from a chat that is not alive can be running, so every screen that would show a spinner for a branch asks this first.

execution.description: The live execution, when Claudio has a process on the chat; also the last of `executions`

activity.description: What that execution is doing right now; `null` whenever none is live

context.description: Null until the chat has had a response

environment.description: Null when nothing has reported it yet

tools.description: What it was started with, when Claudio started it: absent for a chat born in a terminal

pending.description: Messages sent to it that the agent has not taken yet, oldest first, and those lost on the way since; only while Claudio has a record of the chat (docs/chat-delivery.md)

claudioAssistant.description: Set on a chat of the Claudio assistant: it keeps its confinement whenever it is continued, resumed or forked

compact.description: Whether Compact now is offered, and why not; only on a chat read alone, a list does not pay for it

guards.description: The guards on its live process; absent when none runs or the chat is not guarded (docs/plans/guards.md)

policy.description: The policy of a confined API chat, fixed at its creation; null for any other chat (docs/plans/headless-image.md, D14)

teammateReads.description: Which teammates' shared copies its agent may read now (docs/plans/collaborators-agent-access.md); null when it may read none. Only on a chat read alone, decided on its live process

Chat.description: One Claude Code conversation: the root entity of the product. Always exactly one session id, which is also the chat's id. Subagents and workflows are branches of a chat, not chats.

ChatChildren.description: What a chat spawned: branches of it, not chats of their own.

id.description: Id of its transcript inside the chat

sessionId.description: The session it belongs to, which is the chat's id. On every route that reports a subagent, so the one nested in `GET /chats/:id` and the ones `GET /subagents` lists read the same.

startedAt.description: When it was first launched; a resume does not move it (see `runs`)

runs.description: Every stretch it worked, oldest first: one, or more when its parent resumed it

cwd.description: Where it works, when that is not the chat's directory (a worktree)

activity.description: What it is doing right now, from its latest calls; null while it has no open call or has ended

ChatSubagent.description: A branch of a chat that works on its own: its messages live inside the chat's transcript.

ChatAgentStatus.description: An agent has one more state: `waiting`, its turn ended while background work of its own still runs, so it may resume by itself. Not working (no clock, no spinner) and not done.

result.description: What the script returned, once it finished

ChatWorkflow.description: A script that orchestrates subagents inside a chat.

status.description: `stopped`: it was still running when its workflow, or the chat holding it, ended

id.description: Id of its transcript inside the chat, when it has one

source.description: `chat` when this chat's own last process reported it; `folder` when no process of the chat started here (one from a terminal), and it is the last chat's in the same folder

ChatEnvironment.description: What Claude loaded when the chat last started.

open.description: The open compaction or note turn, while there is one

CompactRefusal.description: Why Compact now is not offered; the same codes the 409 carries as `code`

trigger.description: The CLI's word, once its boundary is seen

structuredNote.description: The summary was asked for in the session-note shape

costUsd.description: What the CLI reported for the turn; null when it reported none (never estimated)

error.description: The CLI's text for a failure, or Claudio's for one the CLI did not explain

entries.description: The window of the transcript this page carries, oldest first

from.description: Index of the first entry in `entries` within the whole transcript

total.description: Entries the transcript holds in total, so a caller knows what is still above `from`

stream.description: The chat's stream position when this page was read: open the stream from `seq` to miss nothing said after the read, or from `executionSeq` to see the whole live execution. Null without a live chat.

ChatDetail.description: A page of a chat's transcript with the chat it belongs to.

command.description: The shell command, when it is a backgrounded Bash call

byPerson.description: Sent to the background by the person, not by the model

ownerId.description: The subagent that launched it; null when the chat itself did

ChatBackgroundTaskEntry.description: A background command or agent, listed with the chat that sent it off.

firstPrompt.description: The chat's first prompt, which a screen shows as its title when `title` is only a generated name

ChatRef.description: Which chat a branch belongs to, for the aggregates that list branches of many chats together.

id.description: Id of its transcript inside the chat

sessionId.description: The session it belongs to, which is the chat's id. On every route that reports a subagent, so the one nested in `GET /chats/:id` and the ones `GET /subagents` lists read the same.

startedAt.description: When it was first launched; a resume does not move it (see `runs`)

runs.description: Every stretch it worked, oldest first: one, or more when its parent resumed it

cwd.description: Where it works, when that is not the chat's directory (a worktree)

activity.description: What it is doing right now, from its latest calls; null while it has no open call or has ended

ChatSubagentEntry.description: A subagent, listed with the chat it belongs to.

result.description: What the script returned, once it finished

at.description: When this row was written: the moment it fired, or the moment the wrapper noticed it had skipped

slot.description: The cron slot this run answers, as an ISO time; absent for a run started by hand

error.description: Which field is wrong, when it is not valid

timezone.description: The zone it was read in

publicKey.description: URL-safe base64 VAPID public key, or null when there is none

label.description: What the Settings list calls this install, e.g. "Pixel 8 · Chrome". Derived from the user agent

RegisterPushSubscriptionRequest.description: `POST /push/subscriptions`: the browser's `PushSubscription` JSON plus what this install wants. Sent again whenever the browser rotates the subscription, and an endpoint that is already registered is refreshed rather than duplicated.

NotificationLevel.description: How much a notification may interrupt: a toast in the page, a system notification for a hidden tab, a push to a phone. endpoint.description: Origin of the push service and an elided tail — enough to tell two installs apart

lastSeenAt.description: Last time this install registered or refreshed

PushSubscriptionSummary.description: One registered install. RemovePushSubscriptionRequest.description: `DELETE /push/subscriptions`: the endpoint a browser is unsubscribing, or the id of a row in the list.

SendTestPushRequest.description: `POST /push/test`: one install by endpoint or id, or every registered install when both are omitted.

sent.description: Installs the push service accepted the notification for

removed.description: Installs whose endpoint was gone (404/410) and whose row was deleted

failed.description: Installs the push service refused for any other reason; the row is kept

reason.description: What the push service said about the first install it refused, when it said anything: the status and body of the refusal, so a person reading "it failed" can tell a misconfigured VAPID subject from a phone that is simply offline.

key.description: The dedupe key, shown as the notification `tag` so a chat replaces its own notification

href.description: Path to open, e.g. `/chats/<id>?prompt=<id>`; null when there is nothing but the app to open

url.description: The same place as `href`, as an absolute URL on the tunnel's tailnet address at the moment the push was sent; null while no tunnel is active. PushPayload.description: What travels in a push payload, and deliberately no more: it passes through a push service we do not run, so it holds only what a lock screen shows anyway — no prompt text, no tool arguments, no secrets. It is the small, non-private part of a `NotificationDraft`.

current.description: The CLI on the PATH, as it reports itself; null when it is not installed

issues.description: The tracker issues it was imported from or linked to; absent reads as none
