name.description: The chat's title or the task's name, filled in when read; null when it is gone

chatState.description: Filled in when read, for a chat

taskStatus.description: Filled in when read, for an orchestration task

WorkItemLink.description: A chat, an orchestration task or a document tied to a work item. An item keeps every link, not only the last.

WorkItemLinkKind.description: What a work item can be linked to: what can act on it ( {@link  WorkItemSourceKind } ), and a document of the project (a specification, an architecture decision) tied to it by the Documents module.

WorkItemLinkRole.description:
The part a linked chat, orchestration task or document played in the item's life. The roles past `origin` follow the fixed columns, so they cannot grow with the flow: whichever team role a project puts on a column, its chat is `refine` in `backlog` and `todo`, `work` in `in_progress` and `verify` in `in_review`.

- `origin`: the item was created from it (the chat of "Create a task from this message", or a   document the assistant proposed items from).
- `refine`: refined it before work started; for a document, the specification refinement wrote.
- `work`: worked on it ("Work on it", a node of an orchestration built from it); for a document,   one written while working, such as an architecture decision.
- `verify`: verified it against its acceptance criteria; for a document, the verification report.
- `reference`: tied to it by hand, without playing a part in its life. Documents only, in practice.

`refine`, `work` and `verify` are also what a flow run's chat gets, by its  {@link  FlowStage } ; a client handles every member all the same.

DocumentKind.description: What a document tied to a work item is: `spec`, a specification (the Product Owner's, refining); `adr`, an architecture decision; `report`, a verification report (QA's); `doc`, anything else.

WorkItemWaitReason.description: Why an item waits for the person under the flow by column: `approval`, an agent finished and asks for the move to `done`, which only a person makes; `bounces`, verification sent it back more times than the project allows; `merge`, the person approved it and its pull request is open on GitHub, waiting for the person to merge it there. Each ends when a person moves it; `merge` also ends when the PR is merged (the item reaches `done`) or closed unmerged (back to `approval`).

id.description: The row id the `/change-requests/:id/…` routes take; the server always sends it

host.description: The host that holds it; absent reads as `github` (rows opened before hosts existed)

number.description: Null until the host's CLI answered the create

ref.description: How the host writes the number: `#12` or `!12`; null without a number

base.description: The default branch it is proposed to

ci.description: Null until the watcher first read it

conflicts.description: The paths the update left conflicted, while `phase` is `conflict` or `awaiting-verify`

error.description: Why the last attempt failed: a step or readiness code, and git's or gh's first line of error

checkedAt.description: When the watcher last asked gh about it

fixState.description: The fix of failing checks under way; absent or null when none

fixAttempts.description: Fixes started for `fixHead`, a person's and the decision's together

fixHead.description: The head commit the failures were seen on

addressed.description: The push the last address of review comments made: the head it left and the threads it was handed. Null when it made none (a card taken over drops the fix without one), or after another fix started.

WorkItemPullRequest.description: An item's pull request, the newest of its rows: an item keeps every PR it had, closed ones too.

key.description: What the person reads: `12` on GitHub and GitLab, `PROJ-12` on YouTrack

scope.description: The tracker scope (the repository, for GitHub and GitLab) the issue was imported from. Every call and every closing word about this issue uses it, whatever the project's scope is now; null when it was never recorded, and Claudio then writes nothing to the issue.

externalId.description: The tracker's own id, when it differs from the key

state.description: The state the tracker last reported, in the tracker's words

syncReason.description: Why the last sync failed; null unless `syncState` is `failed`

IssueRef.description: An issue linked to a work item (a `work_item_issues` row).

IssueSyncState.description: Where the last write to the tracker for an issue stands: `none` is nothing synced yet.

HostReason.description: Why a call to a code host did not do what was asked: one taxonomy for every phase. The web words each code; the host's first line travels beside it as the detail.

id.description: Ours and stable: the key changes with the prefix, the id never does

description.description: Markdown. Left out of board and list payloads (the board, the lists and their pages, a chat's items), where it is `''` and  {@link  WorkItem.hasDescription }  says whether there is one: the item's own page fetches it (`GET /work-items/:itemId`, `GET /work-items/by-key/:key`).

hasDescription.description: Whether the item has a description, set wherever `description` is left out. Absent where the description is served whole, where it reads as `description !== ''`.

labels.description: Free text, in the order they were given

epicId.description: Always null for an epic: there is one level of hierarchy

epic.description: The epic, filled in when read, so a card can show its label

rank.description: Order inside its column, compared as plain strings. Opaque to clients, which move an item by naming its neighbour ( {@link  MoveWorkItemRequest } ), so the order a person drags survives.

worktree.description: The item's own git worktree, once something worked on it, on branch `claudio-task/<key>` in lower case

activeLink.description: The chat or orchestration task working on it right now, filled in when read: what makes a card live. Null when nothing is.

bounces.description: Times the verifying role sent it back to `in_progress` in the current round of work, compared with  {@link  ProjectFlowSettings.maxBounces } ; a person moving it starts a new round. Written by the flow by column: absent reads as 0.

waiting.description: What it waits for from the person, which the board shows in the idle colour with a word. Written by the flow by column: absent reads as null, waiting for nothing.

waitingCause.description: Why it waits for bounces when that was the plateau rule (`flow.plateau`) and not the limit, so the board can say "no improvement in two rounds"; absent for every other wait.

pullRequest.description: Its newest pull request; absent or null when it never had one

issues.description: The tracker issues it was imported from or linked to; absent reads as none

closedAt.description: When it last entered `done`; null while it is anywhere else

children.description: For an epic, the items it groups

pullRequestReadiness.description: Whether approving it opens a pull request; absent or null for an item of a project that is not imported

WorkItemDetail.description: One work item with what its page shows beyond the card: `GET /work-items/:itemId`, or `GET /work-items/by-key/:key` for its key (`AGN-12`, in any case; 404 when no project's item has it, since a key prefix is unique among projects).

source.description: The chat or orchestration task an agent wrote it from; null for the person

WorkItemComment.description: Written by the person or by an agent; Markdown, no attachments.

from.description: Null when there was nothing before: `created`, a criterion or a relation added

to.description: Null when there is nothing after: a criterion or a relation removed

cause.description: Set when a chat or an orchestration made the change, rather than someone acting on the item

WorkItemHistoryEntry.description: One change to one field. Written by the service, never by the caller: an update that changes three fields writes three entries.

WorkItemHistoryValue.description: A plain value for a scalar field, the list for `labels`, and a snapshot for everything else.

host.description: The host that holds it; absent reads as `github` (entries written before hosts existed)

ref.description: How the host writes the number: `#12` or `!12`; null without a number

WorkItemHistoryPullRequest.description: A pull request as a history entry records it: opened, conflicted, merged or closed.

WorkItemHistoryRef.description: A referenced thing (an epic, a milestone, a link) as it was when the entry was written, so the history still reads after it is renamed or deleted. For a work item, `key` is composed when read, like every key.

WorkItemHistoryCriterion.description: A criterion as a history entry records it.

detail.description: The raw line git or the CLI answered with, shown in mono beside the worded reason; null when ready

defaultBranch.description: The default branch, when it could be found

host.description: The code host the remote belongs to; null when none could be told

hostname.description: The remote's host name, without user, secret or port; null when there is none

remedy.description: The one thing to do about a not-ready status; null when ready or when nothing can be done

PullRequestReadiness.description: Whether approving an item of this project opens its pull request. Computed from git and the host's CLI and cached for 60 s, so a board read never waits on an auth probe.

PullRequestNotReadyReason.description: Why a project cannot open pull requests (or merge requests); `ready` when it can. "Pull request" in these types means a PR or an MR: the host decides the word.

PullRequestRemedy.description: What a person can do about a not-ready project: a link to follow, never a command to copy.

projectId.description: Left out for every project: the All projects view

labels.description: Items carrying any of these labels

q.description: Searched in the title and the description, and matched against the key

WorkItemFilter.description: What a list, a search or the board is narrowed to. Every field is optional; the values of a list are alternatives (any of them) and fields combine (all of them). In a query string, a list is comma separated.

epicId.description: Must name an epic of the same project; not allowed on an epic

NewAcceptanceCriterion.description: A new entry of the acceptance checklist: an object, so fields can join the text later.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Replaces the whole checklist, in this order

UpdateWorkItemRequest.description: Only the fields present change, and `null` clears a nullable one. The status and the order change through  {@link  MoveWorkItemRequest } , and one criterion is checked through  {@link  CheckAcceptanceCriterionRequest } .

AcceptanceCriterionInput.description: An entry of a replaced checklist: one with an `id` keeps its check, one without is new.

afterId.description: The item it goes right after in the target column; null puts it first, absent puts it last

MoveWorkItemRequest.description: Moves an item to a column and a place in it. The place is named by a neighbour rather than an index, so two people reordering at once do not land items on top of each other.

MoveWorkItemResult.description: A move always succeeds; going over the column's limit is reported, never refused.

limit.description: Null when the column has no limit

count.description: Every item in the column but its epics, whatever the filter: an epic takes no place under the limit

overLimit.description: `count` is over `limit`: shown in the warn colour with a word, never a block

BoardColumnSummary.description: A column without its items: what a move reports.

CreateWorkItemRelationRequest.description: Refused when it points at the item itself or closes a cycle of `blocks`.

documentPath.description: For a `document` link: the document's path, relative to the project

CreateWorkItemLinkRequest.description: Every kind and role is accepted by the contract. A document is tied by hand through `POST /work-items/:itemId/documents` ( {@link  TieDocumentRequest } ), with the role `reference`.

closedAt.description: When it was last closed; null while open

Milestone.description: A named goal (`v0.19`) with no date: open or closed, and how far its work items are.

MilestoneProgress.description: Derived from the milestone's work items, epics left out: they group work, they are not work.

projectId.description: Null for the All projects board, whose columns carry no limit

columns.description: Always the five columns, in  {@link  WorkItemStatus }  order

pullRequestReadiness.description: A project's board: whether approving opens a pull request. Absent on the All projects board

checkout.description: A project's board: its checkout against the default branch; null when the project is not ready

limit.description: Null when the column has no limit

count.description: Every item in the column but its epics, whatever the filter: an epic takes no place under the limit

overLimit.description: `count` is over `limit`: shown in the warn colour with a word, never a block

items.description: The items that pass the filter, in rank order, descriptions left out. The Done column holds only the most recently closed of them, `doneLimit` ( {@link  BoardQuery } ), newest first

more.description: Items that pass the filter and are left out of `items`: "and N more", which asks the board again with a larger `doneLimit`. Only the Done column leaves any out; absent reads as 0.

behind.description: Commits `origin/<default>` has that the checkout lacks

reason.description: Why it was not brought forward; null when it is up to date or can be

BoardCheckout.description: The project's main checkout against the default branch, from local git only (no fetch on read).

CheckoutBehindReason.description: Why the project's main checkout is behind `origin/<default>`: on another branch, carrying changes to tracked files, or holding commits the default branch lacks.

total.description: Every item that passes the filter, across the pages

nextCursor.description: Opaque: pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last

WorkItemPage.description: A page of work items, descriptions left out.

labels.description: Items carrying any of these labels

q.description: Searched in the title and the description, and matched against the key

cursor.description: `nextCursor` of the previous page; absent for the first

WorkItemPageQuery.description: `GET /projects/:id/work-items/page` and `GET /work-items/page` (All projects): the list a page at a time, in the same order as the whole list, with the same filter. `GET /projects/:id/work-items` and `GET /work-items` still answer the whole list as an array.

doneLimit.description: Items of the Done column to hold; default `BOARD_DONE_PAGE`, at most `WORK_ITEMS_PAGE_MAX`

BoardQuery.description: `GET /projects/:id/work-items/board` and `GET /work-items/board` take the filter ( {@link  WorkItemFilter } ) and this. The Done column grows without end, so it is paged: a board holds its newest closed items, and "and N more" asks again with the next multiple of the page. Asking for a larger limit rather than a cursor keeps one board per query, which the event feed refreshes whole.

WorkOnWorkItemRequest.description: What a chat started on a work item may be given. The prompt is built from the item (its title, description and acceptance criteria) and the directory is its worktree, so neither is taken here.

account.description: Id of the  {@link  Account }  to run on. Absent keeps the last execution's on a resume or a fork and lets the rotation policy choose on a new chat; it cannot change on a live chat, so a new value applies from the next process.

provider.description: The provider to run on; the first one in the person's order that can run chats when absent

effort.description: How hard the model thinks (`--effort`): one of  {@link  EFFORT_LEVELS  } , which the API checks; a string here because an agent's own list of levels may name others. Absent keeps the last execution's on a resume or a fork, and takes the recommendation for the model on a new chat. Ignored by a provider that does not declare `effort`. It cannot change on a live chat: a new value applies from the next process.

toolPreset.description: Id of a stored  {@link  ToolPreset } ; an explicit `allowedTools` wins over it. A new chat that names neither this nor `allowedTools` takes the default preset; `null` opts out of it (and, on a resume or a fork, drops the preset the chat had).

mcp.description: MCP servers this chat starts with; absent keeps what it has, `null` goes back to what the CLI loads on its own

claudioMcp.description: Claudio's own MCP server for this chat and the processes after it ( {@link  ChatToolConfig.claudioMcp } ); absent keeps what it has

maxBudgetUsd.description: Ceiling on what this execution may spend

maxTurns.description: Ceiling on the agentic turns this execution may take (`--max-turns`); the CLI enforces it, a whole number of at least 1

fallbackModel.description: The model the chat degrades to on a capacity error (`--fallback-model`)

thinking.description: Thinking mode (`--thinking`); beside `effort`, which stays the usual way to choose how hard the model thinks

maxThinkingTokens.description: Ceiling on thinking tokens (`--max-thinking-tokens`); a live chat changes it with `set_max_thinking_tokens`

thinkingDisplay.description: How thinking is shown in the stream (`--thinking-display`)

resumeSessionAt.description: On a resume, continue at this message of the session, a rewind (`--resume-session-at`), instead of at its end

permissionPrompts.description: `host` sends permissions, questions and plans to the panel; `none`, the default, denies them

workspaceId.description: The workspace (`POST /workspaces`) a new chat runs in, instead of a `cwd`: the chat is a confined API chat ( {@link  ApiChatPolicy } ). Only a new chat takes it.

ChatStartOptions.description: What can be chosen when a process starts on a chat, whether it is new, resumed or a fork.

item.description: The item as it is once the chat started: in its worktree, and in `in_progress` unless a person had it elsewhere

OrchestrateWorkItemsRequest.description: A selection of work items of one project to orchestrate, in the order they were picked.

TriageWorkItemRequest.description: A draft work item to triage: what the person has typed so far.

TriageWorkItemResult.description: `triage` is null unless the point is active and answered in time: the form then stays as it is.

duplicate.description: An open item already seems to cover the draft; the warning does not name which

WorkItemTriage.description: What `board.triage` suggests for a draft: a prefill for the person to keep or change, and a warning. It is the answer of the decision `decisionId`, which the form marks as decided.

externalBlockers.description: Items outside the selection, not done yet, that block an item of it: the graph cannot wait for them

WorkItemOrchestrationDraft.description: A graph to review, not a launched one: one node per item, each naming its item in `workItemId`, and `dependsOn` from the `blocks` relations inside the selection. `POST /orchestrations` launches it.

text.description: The message, which becomes the description

title.description: Default: the message's first line

CreateWorkItemFromMessageRequest.description: Creates a work item in `backlog` from a message of a chat, linked to that chat.

summary.description: Null while nothing has worked on it in a worktree, or once its branch is gone

WorkItemChanges.description: What the item's own branch changed, read from git the way a chat's worktree is.

WorkItemPullRequestResult.description: The answer of `POST /work-items/:itemId/pull-request`: 202 while it is prepared, 200 when one was open already.

enabled.description: The Team module is on; with it off the members are still served, and the client hides them

unassignedAgents.description: Agent files in the project's `.claude/agents/` that no member uses, which "add a member" offers

model.description: Model alias or id of the agent that plays it (`opus`, `sonnet`)

responsibility.description: One line on what it answers for

tools.description: The CLI tools its agent file allows, as  {@link  ProjectTeamRole.tools } ; absent means all of them

writes.description: Paths or globs, relative to the project, the member may write; absent means no restriction of Claudio's own. Enforced on the chats Claudio starts for it through the CLI's permission rules; from a terminal it is only what the agent file says.

commands.description: The shell commands the member may run in the flow's work stage, as patterns the CLI's permission rules take (`npm test`, `pnpm *`: each becomes `Bash(<pattern>)`). Absent means `Bash` is not restricted there, as before; present means only these, and an empty list means no shell at all. The refine and verify stages keep their own tool sets. Checked with  {@link  isTeamCommandPattern  } .

agent.description: Name of the agent file in the project's `.claude/agents/`, without `.md`

effort.description: How hard the member thinks in the flow's runs; absent takes the recommendation for its model and the stage

columns.description: The columns it answers for under the flow, in board order; empty for a role that is only consulted

running.description: Its flow runs working now, oldest first; empty when it is idle

queued.description: How many of its flow runs wait for a free place

lastRun.description: Its latest run that ended, for "refined AGN-47 1 h ago"; null when it never ran

TeamMember.description: A member as `GET /projects/:id/team` serves it: the metadata, its file, and what it is doing.

path.description: Relative to the project: `.claude/agents/<agent>.md`

description.description: As the file's frontmatter says them; null when the file is missing or leaves them out

TeamAgentFileState.description: The member's agent file as it is on disk: `ok`, it matches the metadata; `missing`, it was deleted (the member still shows, and its file can be written again); `drifted`, its frontmatter says something the metadata does not ( {@link  TeamAgentFile.drift } ). A drifted or hand-edited file is reported, never overwritten.

TeamAgentDriftField.description: A frontmatter field of the agent file that disagrees with the member's metadata.

item.description: Filled in when read; null once the item is gone

agent.description: The member's agent file name, as `claude --agent` takes it

effort.description: The effort the run started with; null when none was passed, absent on a run written before it was kept

provider.description: The provider the run's chat is on; `claude-code` on a run written before providers were chosen

waiting.description: Set while the run waits for its provider's limit to reset; null otherwise

step.description: The stage as the person reads it, by its column: `check` is a `refine` in `todo`

column.description: The column the card entered that started it

chatId.description: The chat it runs in; null while queued. A Developer's run continues the item's work chat when there is one

activity.description: What the chat is doing now, filled in when read while it runs

summary.description: The result's summary, once it ended with one

error.description: Why it failed or was cancelled, in English, as the core or the CLI said it; null otherwise

cause.description: Why it failed or was cancelled, as a code to word; null otherwise, and on an old run whose error reads as none

retryOf.description: The failed run a person retried with this one (`POST /flow-runs/:runId/retry`); null for a run a card entering its column started

queuedBy.description: Who queued it when it was not a card entering its column: `person` for a run a person started from the Flow screen's "start the waiting cards" (`POST /projects/:id/flow/start-waiting`). Null for a run a card's entry queued, and for a retry, which `retryOf` names.

retriedBy.description: On a run that did not pass, the next run of the same step on the item, whatever started it (a retry or the card entering the column again): what the person's retry, or the flow, did next. Null until there is one.

retryable.description: Whether `POST /flow-runs/:runId/retry` would queue it again now: it failed, nothing has run that step on the item since, the item is still in the run's column, and the flow is on with a member answering for the column.

restarts.description: Times a restart cut it off and it went on in its chat; past `MAX_FLOW_RESTARTS` it fails

continuations.description: Times the flow sent it back to its chat because its turn ended with work still owed (no structured result, uncommitted changes, or a last message that offers, asks or announces instead of doing): at most `MAX_CONTINUATIONS`, after which the result it has is judged as it is

language.description: The person's language, which the first line of its chat's prompt (`<Role> · <KEY>`, the title the chat is listed by) is written in, kept so a restart words it the same. Absent on a run stored before it was kept, which reads as `en`.

checks.description: On a run that fixed failing checks, what the Developer decided about each; absent on other runs

guardBlocks.description: Tool calls the guard blocked in this run; filled on read from `guard_events`

FlowRun.description: One run of a team member on a work item, queued, running or ended. Rows, so it survives a restart.

FlowRunState.description: `queued` waits for a place under `maxParallel`; `running` has its chat; `ended` has an outcome.

FlowRunRef.description: Another run as a run refers to it: enough to say what it did and open its chat.

locations.description: Where the Developer changed things for this check, as `path:line` (at most 20, each at most 200 characters)

stopped.description: Set when the Developer stopped before the check was fixed, and why

FlowCheckVerdict.description: The Developer's call on one failing check of a fix: this branch caused it, did not, or it is unclear.

TeamFromTemplateRequest.description:
Writes the members of the project's template (`ProjectTemplate.team`). The person accepts them one by one, so `roles` names the ones accepted; absent means every role of the template. An agent file that already exists is kept as it is, and a role already on the team is left alone.

`POST /projects/:id/team/from-template` answers the whole  {@link  Team } : with 201 when it added at least one member, and with 200 when nothing changed (every role was already on the team), like the other creating routes. Sending it twice is harmless either way.

model.description: Model alias or id of the agent that plays it (`opus`, `sonnet`)

responsibility.description: One line on what it answers for

writes.description: Where a template's role may write, as  {@link  ProjectTeamMember.writes }  reads it; absent means no limit of Claudio's

commands.description: Absent or null leaves the shell unrestricted in the work stage ( {@link  ProjectTeamMember.commands } )

tools.description: Absent or null leaves every tool allowed ( {@link  ProjectTeamMember.tools } ); at most 30 names, each a tool name with an optional `(pattern)`

effort.description: Absent or null takes the recommendation for the member's model and the stage ( {@link  ProjectTeamMember.effort } )

createFile.description: Write a starting agent file for the role when there is none; an existing file is never overwritten

PutTeamMemberRequest.description: Creates or replaces a member's metadata (`PUT /projects/:id/team/:agent`). The agent file itself is edited through `/config/resources/agents/:name?project=`.

queued.description: In the order they will start

ProjectFlow.description: `GET /projects/:id/flow`: what the flow is doing in a project now.

total.description: Every run that passes the filter, across the pages

nextCursor.description: Opaque: pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last

FlowRunPage.description: A page of a project's flow runs, newest first.

total.description: 0 while the flow, the Team module or the Board module is off

columns.description: In board order; only the columns with at least one waiting card

FlowWaiting.description: `GET /projects/:id/flow/waiting`: the cards a flow switched on would not start by itself. A card waits when it is not an epic nor done, its column has a role with a member playing it, it has no run queued or running, and, in todo, it was not refined and left unchanged since.

role.description: The team role that answers for the column, matching  {@link  ProjectTeamRole.role }

FlowWaitingColumn.description: One column of  {@link  FlowWaiting } : how many of its cards wait, and the role that answers for it.

queued.description: Runs queued, one per waiting card

startingNow.description: Of those, how many the project's `maxParallel` lets start now: `min(queued, maxParallel − running)`

waiting.description: `queued − startingNow`: they start as places come free

day.description: The server's local `YYYY-MM-DD`; tomorrow the card is under that day's cap again

FlowSpendPass.description: A card's pass past the daily spend cap: the local day it is good for.

criteria.description: Verification only: every acceptance criterion of the item, each judged on its own

FlowRunResult.description: The structured result every flow run ends with, through the CLI's `--json-schema`. `summary` becomes the member's comment on the item; `verdict` is QA's only.

FlowVerdict.description: QA's verdict: `pass` leaves the item waiting for the person's approval, `fail` sends it back to `in_progress`.

id.description: The criterion's id, as the run's prompt lists it

note.description: What was checked, or what is missing

needsPerson.description: No flow run can check it: it needs a push, a pull request, a tool or service the run does not have, or a person's eyes. It is left unchecked for the person who approves the item and does not reject the run (refines decision 18).

FlowCriterionResult.description: QA's judgement of one acceptance criterion. A met criterion is checked on the item as the agent; the run passes only when every criterion of the item is met or needs a person.

reason.description: Why the team should remember it

FlowMemoryProposal.description: A memory entry a flow run proposes, as its result carries it.

path.description: Relative to the project, inside the documents folder (`docs/specs/agn-28-board.md`)

FlowRunDocument.description: A document a flow run wrote in the item's worktree, reported so Claudio ties it to the item.

handed.description: What a flow run is handed: the newest entries that fit the cap

nextBefore.description: Pass as `before` for the next page; null on the last

text.description: Markdown; for `closed`, the item's title as it was

item.description: Filled in when read; null when there is no item or it is gone

author.description: Who wrote or proposed it: the person, or the agent and its role

approvedBy.description: Who approved it: the move to `done` for `closed`, the proposal for `memory`; null for what a person wrote

documentPath.description: A document it refers to (an architecture decision), relative to the project

sources.description: For `closed`: the chats and orchestration tasks that worked on the item

JournalEntry.description: One entry of a project's journal, Claudio's own record of decisions and closed items. The newest are handed to every flow run with `--append-system-prompt`.

CreateJournalEntryRequest.description: An entry written by hand. `closed` and `memory` are Claudio's to write.

item.description: Filled in when read; null when there is no item or it is gone

approvedText.description: What was written, when the person edited it before approving; null otherwise

rejectReason.description: Why it was rejected, when the person said

journalEntryId.description: The journal entry an approval to the journal wrote

lesson.description: Filled in when read, for `target.kind === 'lesson'`: the lesson and its evidence, which the card shows

lessonId.description: Set for an `instructions` proposal made from a lesson, so the lesson can be retired once it is approved

MemoryProposal.description: A memory entry a team member proposed. Nothing is written until the person approves it.

key.description: `L-<seq>`, stable, what runs and people refer to

trigger.description: When it applies: English, starting with "When", at most 160 characters

action.description: What to do or avoid then: at most 240 characters, behaviour only

effectiveConfidence.description: After decay, as of the read; what delivery compares

delivered.description: Whether it is handed to runs now

mechanical.description: About one command, tool or path: a candidate for a guard rule (plans/guards.md)

conflictsWithInstructions.description: The miner said it conflicts with CLAUDE.md

contradicts.description: The lesson it contradicts, when the person kept both

overrides.description: A project lesson that overrides this global one in its project

promotedFrom.description: For a global lesson: the project lesson it was promoted from

alsoInProjects.description: Active lessons in other projects that say the same (similarity rule), counted when read

instructionsProposalId.description: The pending or decided `instructions` proposal made from it

LessonStatus.description: proposed: waits for the person; active: handed to runs; retired: kept, not handed; rejected: refused, never proposed again; superseded: replaced by its global copy

LessonRetiredReason.description: Why a lesson stopped being handed

quote.description: The person's own words, as written (any language), redacted; empty for a denial without a message

context.description: What the agent had just done, in English, redacted: "Edit src/cart.ts", "Bash: npm install"

Read, it is the configured allowlist: the environment's hosts followed by the ones added in the UI. maxConcurrentRuns.description: How many runs may work at once; a change applies to the next run, without a restart

defaultPermissionMode.description: The `--permission-mode` of a run that does not ask for one; applies to the next run

setupSeen.description: The setup assistant was finished or skipped. Kept here rather than in the browser so a second browser, a phone or the desktop app does not ask again. It replaces `providersStepSeen`: that stored value and its variable, `CLAUDIO_PROVIDERS_STEP_SEEN`, still count.

dailySpendCapUsd.description: What all of Claudio's automation may spend in a local day, in USD, summing the cost the CLI reports for each result. evalsPhase2.description: Instruction evals, Phase 2: pressure levels, judged expectations, the promotion gate and case drafting. Off by default; while off, those routes answer 409 `evals-phase2-off`. Phase 1 evals are not affected.

openaiToolCallTimeoutMinutes.description: How long the OpenAI-compatible surface holds a client's tool call, in minutes, from the end of the turn that handed it over until the client's next request brings the result. UpdateAppSettingsRequest.description: `PUT /settings/app`: the settings to change, and only those. SettingsState.description: `GET /settings/state`: every server-side setting a row can reset, by its `data-setting` id

changed.description: The stored value differs from the default: the row shows "Changed · Reset"

sources.description: `env` is read-only here (`CLAUDIO_TUNNEL_PORT`); `file` was saved from the app

startWithClaudio.description: Open the tunnel whenever Claudio starts; off unless the person turns it on

port.description: The HTTPS port of Claudio's Serve rule on the tailnet name, 1024–65535, 8444 by default. Changed only while the tunnel is stopped or failed, and read-only where `CLAUDIO_TUNNEL_PORT` sets it

UpdateTunnelSettingsRequest.description: `PUT /tunnel/settings`: the settings to change, and only those.

shell.description: The shell's path; `null` is the person's login shell

TerminalServerFrame.description: Control frames from the server to the view. Output is a binary frame and carries no type.

refused.description: The gate's reason when the attempt was refused

rotation.description: What happens at a usage limit; absent on a file written before it, read as the defaults

toChat.description: The new chat; null for a wait

decisionId.description: The decision point's answer, when `decidedBy` is `decision`

resetsAt.description: ISO time the wait ends; null when unknown or not a wait

email.description: Pre-fills the email the CLI asks for

device.description: Whether the vendor documents a device-code sign-in Claudio runs

needsHost.description: Whether a host name is part of the sign-in: `gh` and `glab` name one, YouTrack an address

limitedUntil.description: While the host's rate limit is used up: when Claudio may read again; the state is the last one it had

signature.description: Ed25519 by the `owner` of the previous version, or by this version's own `owner` for version 1; hex

RosterVersion.description: One signed version of a group's roster. Canonical bytes are RFC 8785 over the version without `signature`; `groupId` and `prevHash` are the sha256 of such bytes, hex.

RosterMember.description: One person's install in a roster version. The owner is listed too, with role `owner`.

id.description: The group id: sha256 of the signed genesis

isOwner.description: Whether this install is the owner, and so may invite, accept, remove and transfer

members.description: The head version's members, the owner first

frozen.description: The owner's install is gone (its key is lost): the group can no longer change. Known on the install that held the group as its owner and holds another key now (a vault lost or restored apart from the data); to a member, the owner only looks offline.

conflict.description: The owner's install found two versions with the same number and different hashes (§3.3). Shown as an error until the owner signs a higher version over it; null when the chain is consistent.

joinRequestCount.description: Pending joins relayed to the owner; always 0 for a member

Group.description: A group this install belongs to, as `GET /collaborators/groups` lists it.

hash.description: sha256 of the head version's canonical bytes, hex

RosterHead.description: The head of a group's chain: what every connection starts by comparing.

presence.description: Null on the install's own entry

GroupMember.description: A roster member with what this install knows about it now.

pendingJoins.description: Requests to join that wait for an owner, or ended unanswered or denied until dismissed, so the page shows them after a reload

CreateGroupRequest.description: `POST /collaborators/groups`: the creator becomes the owner, at version 1.

text.description: The text the invitee pastes; the QR code encodes the same text

JoinGroupResult.description: The answer to a join: `joined` when the owner signed in the same round trip, `pending` when a member stored the request until the owner is back.

TransferGroupOwnershipRequest.description: `PUT /collaborators/groups/:id/owner`: the current owner signs a version naming the new one.

groups.description: The groups the project is shared with

shareKey.description: The key in use: the stored one, or the default until something is stored

defaultShareKey.description: The key computed from the repository, so the section can offer to go back to it

remote.description: The remote the key comes from; null when the repository has none (`local/<hex>`)

remotes.description: Every remote of the repository, for the `Select` when there are several

subpath.description: Inside the repository, for a project in a subdirectory (`--show-prefix`); null at its root

keyInUse.description: Another project of this install already shares this key: the toggles stay off until it is edited

kinds.description: What is included; not chosen per project

seenAs.description: What a collaborator sees as the project's name and remote

agentsMayRead.description: Teammates' agents may read what this project shares (the sharer's flag, on by default)

agentReads.description: This project's chats may read what teammates share into it (off by default)

url.description: The remote's URL with credentials dropped

shareKey.description: The key computed from this remote

SharingRemote.description: A git remote of the project, as the Sharing section offers it.

shareKey.description: An edited key: `[a-z0-9._/#-]{3,200}`, refused with 400 otherwise

remote.description: Recomputes the key from this remote; null goes back to the default remote

UpdateProjectSharingRequest.description: `PUT /projects/:id/sharing`: the fields to change, and only those.

ShareKeyInUseError.description: The 409 body of `PUT /projects/:id/sharing` when another project already shares the key.

owner.description: The sharing install's endpoint id, the `:owner` of the routes

ownerName.description: The person's display name: the page groups by it, then by `ownerLabel`

groupIds.description: The groups through which this install sees it

shareId.description: `sha256(shareKey)`, 32 hex characters: a share key holds `/` and `#`, so routes use this

matches.description: Local projects whose default key equals `shareKey`; several for two clones

linkedProjectId.description: The local project it was linked to by hand; null when it was not

agentsMayRead.description: The sharer lets teammates' agents read it. Off, neither the assistant nor any chat of this install gets the copy; the person still reads it here

SharedProject.description: A project a teammate's install shares with this one (`GET /collaborators/shared`).

LinkSharedProjectRequest.description: `PUT /collaborators/shared/:owner/:shareId/link`: shows the shared project inside a local one.

branch.description: The worktree's branch, when the chat ran in one

live.description: An agent is working in it on the owner's machine now: the row carries the live rail

activity.description: What that agent is doing, while `live`

subagents.description: The subagents and workflow agents whose transcripts the CLI kept beside the chat's; absent in a copy from an older install

SharedChat.description: A teammate's chat, as copied: what its row and its header need, nothing of the owner's process.

agentId.description: The CLI's id of the agent, which names its transcript

workflowRunId.description: The workflow run (`wf_…`) a workflow agent belongs to; null for a subagent

size.description: Bytes of its transcript on the owner's machine when the chat was read

SharedSubagent.description: A subagent or workflow agent of a teammate's chat, as copied: what opens its transcript from the call that launched it. Its transcript is pulled with the chat's.

from.description: Index of the first entry in `entries` within the copied transcript

SharedTranscriptPage.description: `GET /collaborators/shared/:owner/:shareId/chats/:chatId/transcript`: a window of the copied transcript.

from.description: Index of the first entry in `entries` within the copied transcript

SharedAgentTranscriptPage.description: `GET /collaborators/shared/:owner/:shareId/chats/:chatId/subagents/:agentId`: a window of a copied subagent's transcript.

SharedMemoryFile.description: A memory file of the owner's project, as copied.

path.description: Relative to the project

sha256.description: The content is the blob of this hash, fetched from the owner on first open

SharedDocument.description: A file of the owner's documents folder, or the project's `CLAUDE.md`, from the owner's working tree.

SharedArtifact.description: An artifact of the owner's project: an orchestration's result, an upload of a shared chat, a plan draft.

chatId.description: The chat whose token read it

tool.description: The MCP tool that asked, as it named itself; the route's summary when it named none

owner.description: The sharing install, the `:owner` of the routes

kind.description: Null for the list of shared projects, which reads no one copy

recordIds.description: The records read: a chat's id for its transcript, the ids a list answered

AgentReadEntry.description: What an agent read of a copy, one row per read: `GET /collaborators/agent-reads`.
